prompt:
I need the front end for Roomturn. A room-readiness system for mid-sized hotels that runs on the back-office wall display, where housekeeping, the front desk and maintenance all update and watch the same picture of every room's status.

Who's using it: Marisol, the housekeeping supervisor at a 180-room downtown hotel. She stands at the wall display with the front-desk lead, Kenji, while attendants and the maintenance tech update rooms from the floors on their phones.

What they're doing right now: It's 10:40 a.m. on a Tuesday, and a pharmaceutical conference group of 46 rooms starts arriving at 1 p.m., with 23 of them asking for early check-in. Marisol and Kenji are deciding together which rooms to put first in line for cleaning and which arrivals to assign to them. Meanwhile, attendants are marking rooms clean and the maintenance tech is closing out a broken AC unit. They need to see who changed what in the last few minutes, avoid both assigning the same room, and make sure only Marisol can mark a room inspected and only the front desk can assign a guest.

What's in the system at this point: 180 rooms over floors 3–12, each with a type (king, double queen, suite), a status (occupied, due out, vacant dirty, cleaning in progress, clean, inspected, out of order), its assigned attendant and the last change with time and author (e.g. '714 marked clean by Ana P., 10:36'). 9 attendants on shift, each with 12–16 rooms and a progress count. 61 departures today, 38 already checked out. 4 rooms out of order (e.g. 908, AC compressor, Dmitri working on it, estimated 11:30). Group block 'Veralis Pharma Summit': 46 rooms, 23 early-arrival requests ranked by loyalty tier, 7 needing an accessible room. Present right now: Marisol and Kenji at the display, plus 6 attendants and Dmitri active on their phones.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
